96.s: Growing up among many groups on the West Side, he recalls his mother forbidding the boys to use a racial slur and insisting on 'colored people'.
96.ch: Chicago boyhood and the Austin High Gang
96.q: Yes, but I haven't told you something to actually go way back before this. I'd like to mention this. That my first influence that I recognized, the two, my brother and I did. You see I was born on Lake and Polina Street on the West Side of Chicago and it was a mixed neighborhood. We had everyone.…

168.t: Little segregation in Englewood; first noticing it on the way to Boston
168.s: Asked about Englewood's mix, Stewart says he noticed no segregation at home but first saw it on the train and in Boston stations and restaurants.
168.q: That's about the way it was around home in Englewood. There wasn't really any segregation. What I mean, I didn't notice it, and especially at that age I was just like all of the fellows, you know, and girls in school. You know what I mean.

86.t: Mixed schools, segregated city in Columbus
86.s: Schools were integrated but theaters, restaurants and neighborhoods were not, and he could not hear Armstrong downtown.
86.q: And she asked the manager of the hotel, which was the Palace, downtown, blacks couldn't go -- we had mixed schools there but after school was out you'd have to go to your neighborhood and the whites go to their neighborhoods. But mixed school was very -- it played an important part in my life, the…

455.t: Segregation at the state fair and Juneteenth
455.s: Black visitors got only one day at the fair, called Juneteenth; Budd and Keg got in because their father demonstrated Studebakers.
455.q: All the other -- yeah, the 19th of June. And look, it was so segregated that you know that the Fourth of July was really the day for the Emancipation, but they wouldn't let the Negroes have Fourth of July, so they gave them the 19th of June.

171.t: Segregation in Missouri and Kansas schools; Reno Club
171.s: Kansas schools were integrated apart from Kansas City, Kansas, while Missouri clubs kept the races apart.
171.ch: Western University and Kansas City nightlife
171.q: Yeah, and you couldn't sit with them unless the boss really just went on and bent over backwards and said, "Come over here and talk," you know, something like that. Now, like the Reno Club, they would go get Basie or Joe Jones or somebody and come on, bring 'em over to the table and sit with them…

239.t: Integration in Memphis and Fisk; touring homecomings with the Collegians
239.s: Jones recalls the integrated atmosphere at Le Moine and Fisk and the Collegians' homecoming dates at several universities.
239.q: Uh-huh. Because all the homes we went to were -- not all of them, but they respected my father highly. And these were white homes. There was no problem, no nothing. We had a ball, you know? It was no -- nothing like what came up later. Now they say it's really improved greatly. Like at Fisk…
